record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: In 3d N = 4 theories, Higgs and Coulomb branches are related by symplectic duality, and certain phase diagrams are related by inversion. Is there a conceptual or structural relation between symplectic duality and inversion of phase diagrams?

evidence.quote: Question 3. Can we find any relation between symplectic duality and inversions of phase diagrams?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In three-dimensional N=4 supersymmetric gauge theories the moduli space of supersymmetric vacua decomposes into a Higgs branch and a Coulomb branch, each of which is a (singular) symplectic variety stratified by its symplectic leaves. The Hasse diagram of this stratification, with vertices labelled by elementary transverse slices (either Kleinian ADE singularities or minimal nilpotent orbit closures of simple Lie algebras), encodes the partial Higgsing/phase structure of the branch and is therefore called the phase diagram of the branch.

Two structures are defined on such theories:

1. Symplectic duality: a pairing of conical symplectic singularities (X, X^!) which, for many 3d N=4 theories, identifies X with the Higgs branch and X^! with the Coulomb branch of the same theory; equivalently it is an equivalence between certain categories O attached to X and X^!.

2. Inversion of phase diagrams: an involution on Hasse diagrams which reverses the partial order and simultaneously exchanges the labels by swapping each Kleinian ADE singularity of type g with the closure of the minimal nilpotent orbit of the simple Lie algebra of type g (and vice versa).

Problem. Determine whether there is a conceptual or structural relation between symplectic duality and inversion of phase diagrams. Concretely, formulate and prove (or disprove) precise conditions on a 3d N=4 theory T under which the phase diagrams of the Higgs and Coulomb branches of T are exchanged by the inversion involution exactly when those branches are symplectic dual, and explain the underlying mathematical mechanism (e.g. in terms of categories O, symplectic resolutions, or magnetic quivers) relating the two notions.
artifact.category_tag: Symplectic duality and 3d N=4 Coulomb/Higgs branches
artifact.status_search_result: The notion of Hasse-diagram inversion conjecturally relating Higgs and Coulomb branch phase diagrams was introduced by Grimminger–Hanany (JHEP 09 (2020) 159), and subsequent surveys (e.g. Kamnitzer 2022 on symplectic duality; the 2024 Perimeter workshop on symplectic singularities and magnetic quivers; Bourget et al. 2025 on 3d mirrors and phase diagrams) continue to discuss the relationship as conjectural, with no general conceptual identification of symplectic duality with phase-diagram inversion established. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Hasse diagrams for 3d N=4 quiver gauge theories — Inversion and the full moduli space
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces inverting a Hasse diagram and conjectures that Coulomb and Higgs branch Hasse diagrams of certain theories are related through this operation.
status_evidence.claim: Inversion of phase diagrams is a conjectural operation relating Higgs and Coulomb branches; no proven equivalence to symplectic duality is given.

status_evidence.title: Symplectic resolutions, symplectic duality, and Coulomb branches (Kamnitzer 2022)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of symplectic duality and Coulomb branch constructions; no identification with Hasse-diagram inversion is asserted.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys treat symplectic duality and inversion as distinct, with their conceptual relation still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: 3d Mirrors and Phase Diagrams of Abelian Gauge Theories (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Continued investigation of how mirror symmetry/symplectic duality acts on phase (Hasse) diagrams in 3d N=4 theories.
status_evidence.claim: The relation between symplectic duality and phase-diagram inversion is still being explored in current literature.
